entries.reason: An arcade divides a structure's front into one to twenty-four equal bays; more would leave piers too close for an opening a person passes. The least opening below refuses a front too short for its bays.

entries.reason: The covered walk behind the arches is from 2 m, room for two people to pass under it clear of the piers and the door, to 12 m, the deepest loggia the style kit's arcade piece draws.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica world kinds; see the entry reasons

entries.reason: Authored: each pier between two arches is 800 mm wide, a stout masonry pier for a ground storey carrying the storeys above; half a pier stands against each end wall, so every bay is the same.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica world kinds; see the entry reasons

entries.reason: Authored: an arch's opening stops 600 mm under the ground storey's ceiling, for the arch's head and the floor above it; the opening is never lower than a door's 2,100 mm, so a storey under 2,700 mm takes no arcade.

licence.content_source: Authored for Exulanica world kinds; see the entry reasons

entries.reason: An arch is at least 1,500 mm wide: a walker is 680 mm across (a 340 mm radius), so a way through stays clear of both piers with room to spare, and two people can pass in one arch.

entries.reason: An arcade runs along a structure's front, or along its front and its back so the ground storey is open on both long sides, as a hall with an aisle on each side is; each side has its own covered walk and a door at the walk's back.
